kurz: How second-rate mortgages became AAA securities, why a single insolvency brought the global financial system to a standstill and which legal rules have applied since then.

bloecke.md:
The 2008 crisis is often portrayed as a property crisis, but this view explains too little. House prices in the US fell from mid-2006 onwards. Credit losses of this order of magnitude can explain a recession, but not a situation in which banks, in October 2008, would no longer lend to one another even overnight.

A credit problem turned into a standstill of the financial system because three circumstances coincided. The risks were contained in securities with so many layers that nobody knew any longer where they lay. They were held by financial institutions working with 3% to 5% equity. Their funding ran for a few days, whereas their investments ran for decades. Each of these circumstances seemed reasonable taken on its own. The course of the crisis was determined more by their interaction than by the trigger.

## Subprime loans and the lending business model

Subprime refers to mortgage loans to borrowers with weak creditworthiness. Between 2004 and 2006, they accounted for around one fifth of all new US residential mortgages. Contracts with a low initial rate for two years and a significantly higher rate afterwards were common. For some of the loans, proof of income was waived.

The change in the business model weighed more heavily than the quality of the individual loans. In the classic model, the bank keeps the loan on its balance sheet and bears any default itself, which is why it checks the borrower. In the *originate to distribute* model (lending in order to sell the loans on), the intermediary earns money from making the loan and passes the claim on. At every stage of the chain, income depended on volume, and the quality of the loans played no part in it.

The whole construction rested on the assumption of rising house prices. As long as prices rise, even an overstretched borrower can refinance the loan or sell the house at a profit, and the loan does not default. If prices fall, this way out disappears for all borrowers at once.

schritte.text: A broker arranges the mortgage and receives the commission when the contract is signed. The broker does not bear the risk from the later performance of the loan.

An investment bank buys thousands of such loans and transfers them to a [[Special purpose vehicle (SPV)|special purpose vehicle]]. This is a separate company without staff whose sole purpose is to hold this loan pool.

The pool's cash flows are divided into ranks. Interest and repayments flow from the top down, while defaults are allocated from the bottom up. This division is the central element of [[Securitisation|securitisation]].

A rating agency rates each [[Tranche|tranche]] separately. In this way, a pool of second-rate loans mostly produces securities with the top rating of AAA. The agency is paid by the issuer, not by the buyer.
The hard-to-sell middle tranches of many pools are pooled again and tranched again. The result is called a CDO (collateralised debt obligation). This second bundle also produces an AAA tranche.

The buyers are insurers, pension funds, Landesbanken (German regional state banks) and special purpose vehicles of other banks. They are often institutions that, under their own investment guidelines, may only buy AAA-rated securities.

bloecke.md:
## Default correlation and the AAA rating

Tranching itself is harmless. It distributes known risks among investors with different capacities to bear risk. A senior tranche covering 80% of the pool only loses money when more than 20% of the pool defaults. How likely this is depends on a single variable, the correlation of defaults. It describes how strongly the defaults of the individual loans are linked to each other.

If the loans are largely independent of each other, a simultaneous default of one fifth is practically ruled out, and the AAA rating is justified. If, on the other hand, all loans depend on the same cause, here house prices across the whole country, such a default becomes almost certain as soon as those prices fall. The valuation models worked with correlations from a period in which US house prices had never fallen nationwide. From the peak in 2006 to the low in 2012, the national price index lost just over a quarter, and around a third in the large metropolitan areas.

bloecke.titel: How a pool loss is distributed across the tranches (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: The assumed structure is 80% senior (AAA), 15% mezzanine and 5% equity. The figures are percentage points of the whole pool. Up to a pool loss of 20%, the top tranche remains untouched; above that, it shares in the loss.

bloecke.md: Between the fourth and the fifth bar, the position of the AAA tranche changes fundamentally. At a pool loss of 20%, it is intact; at 28%, it bears 8 percentage points of the pool. Relative to its own nominal amount of 80, that is a loss of 10%. Such a security therefore does not deteriorate gradually. It remains untouched up to a threshold and is hit beyond it. This behaviour at a threshold distinguishes a structured tranche from an ordinary bond with the same rating.

bloecke.titel: Two flaws in the rating system
bloecke.md: The first flaw was a conflict of interest. The rating agency was paid by the issuer, who could keep changing the structure until the desired AAA came out. The second flaw lay in the scale. The same symbol stood for a German federal bond, backed by a state, and for a CDO tranche whose rating rested on a model calculation. When the agencies began downgrading in large numbers from July 2007, many buyers immediately lost permission to hold these securities at all. The downgrades thus forced sales into a market in which nobody was buying any more.

## Leverage, maturities and illiquidity

In 2007, the large US investment banks worked with balance sheet leverage of about 30 to 1, some with even higher leverage. More important than this ratio was the funding. A considerable part of the balance sheet was refinanced overnight, through repurchase agreements (repos) against collateral or through short-term money market paper. The run on the banks therefore came from professional lenders and hardly from customers at the counter. The queue outside the British bank Northern Rock on 14 September 2007, of which there are well-known pictures, was an exception.

German banks were affected early. IKB Deutsche Industriebank had to be rescued at the end of July 2007 because its special purpose vehicle Rhineland Funding could no longer place its short-term paper. The bank had provided guarantees for a company that formally did not belong to it. A few weeks later, Sachsen LB also ran into difficulties, more than a year before the Lehman insolvency.

bloecke.titel: Effect of a haircut on collateral (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.md:
A bank has total assets of $600 billion and $20 billion of equity. That corresponds to leverage of 30 to 1 and an equity ratio of 3.3%. A loss in value of 3.3% would, arithmetically, wipe out the equity.

Payment problems, however, usually arise earlier. Suppose that $300 billion of this balance sheet is financed through repos and the lenders raise the haircut from 2% to 10%. The bank then has to back the same position overnight with $24 billion more of its own funds, that is, with more than its entire equity. No realised loss is needed for this. It is enough for the lenders to change their assessment of the collateral.

bloecke.titel: The 19 months from the start of the crisis to the low
bloecke.unter: Thirteen months passed between the freezing of the interbank market and the Lehman insolvency. Investors who expected a quick end to the crisis in 2007 were wrong.

ereignisse.text: IKB has to be rescued because its special purpose vehicle can no longer place money market paper. Sachsen LB follows shortly afterwards.
BNP Paribas suspends redemptions of units in three funds because their securities can no longer be valued. On the same day, the ECB provides €94.8 billion in overnight liquidity.
The first bank run in Britain for around 140 years. It takes place outside the branches, not on the capital market.
Emergency sale to JPMorgan, initially at $2 per share. The Fed takes on risks from around $30 billion of hard-to-sell securities. Market participants now expect banks in distress to be rescued.
One year after the crisis began, the ECB raises its main refinancing rate to 4.25% because of inflation driven by the oil price. Ten months later, it stands at 1.00%.
The two mortgage financiers are placed under government conservatorship. Their securities are held on the balance sheets of central banks and banks worldwide.
Bankruptcy filing with total assets of around $600 billion, the largest insolvency in US history. Merrill Lynch is sold to Bank of America on the same weekend.

The insurer AIG receives a credit line of $85 billion, which is later increased to around $180 billion. The money market fund Reserve Primary falls below one dollar per unit because it holds Lehman paper worth around $785 million.

The House of Representatives initially rejects the rescue package, and the S&P 500 loses 8.8% that day. On 3 October, TARP is passed with around $700 billion. In Germany, the deposit guarantee follows on 5 October, and on 17 October the Financial Market Stabilisation Act (Finanzmarktstabilisierungsgesetz) with the SoFFin fund of €480 billion.
The DAX closes at its low of 3,666.41 points, and the S&P 500 reaches its lowest level one trading day later. The loss from the peak is 55.0% and 56.8% respectively.

bloecke.md:
## The Lehman weekend and the consequences on the money market

To this day, it is disputed why Lehman collapsed but AIG, one day later, did not. What is known is that no buyer was found for Lehman and that the British supervisor would not allow a takeover by Barclays without a shareholder vote. The Fed cited a lack of collateral for emergency financing, and the political willingness for further rescues had been exhausted after Bear Stearns, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. AIG, by contrast, had sold credit default insurance through a London unit on the securities that were held on balance sheets all over the world. A default by AIG would have hit all counterparties at the same time.

After that, the contagion spread to further parts of the economy mainly through the money market. When the Reserve Primary Fund fell below one dollar per unit, investors withdrew money from money market funds. These funds were the largest buyers of short-term corporate paper. As a result, even industrial companies that had nothing to do with subprime suddenly could no longer obtain bridge financing for their wages. The spread of unsecured interbank loans over US government securities was normally two to five tenths of a percentage point and rose to over four percentage points in October 2008.

## Rescue measures and their costs

Governments intervened in three ways: with guarantees for liabilities, with fresh equity in exchange for stakes, and with liquidity from the central bank. The Fed's total assets grew from $881 billion at the start of 2008 to $2,121 billion at the start of 2009. They thus rose to around 2.4 times their level within one year and grew by more than in the preceding sixty years of normal monetary policy.

In Germany, Chancellor Merkel and Finance Minister Steinbrück declared savings deposits safe on 5 October 2008. This political pledge had no legal basis and worked because savers believed it. Twelve days later, the Financial Market Stabilisation Act created the Special Fund for Financial Market Stabilisation (Sonderfonds Finanzmarktstabilisierung, SoFFin) with a framework of €480 billion, of which €400 billion was for guarantees. Hypo Real Estate was rescued and, in 2009, became the first bank in the Federal Republic to be nationalised. Several Landesbanken transferred securities to wind-down agencies (Abwicklungsanstalten).

In this way, bank debt became government debt. The debt ratio of today's 27 EU member states rose from 65.1% of GDP (2008) to 75.7% (2009). This increase was the precondition for the euro crisis two years later.

bloecke.titel: Key interest rates of the Fed and the ECB, 2006 to 2010
bloecke.unter: The ECB was still raising its key interest rate in July 2008, while the Fed had been cutting for ten months. The steps show documented decision dates.

bloecke.md:
## Consequences for investors and the economy

The S&P 500 lost a total of 56.8% from 9 October 2007 to 9 March 2009 and only regained its previous level on 28 March 2013, five and a half years after the peak. The DAX fell from 8,151.57 points (13 July 2007) to 3,666.41 points (6 March 2009), a decline of 55.0%. In 2008 alone it lost 40.37%, and it reached a new all-time high in May 2013. Investors who were still invested at the low then needed a price gain of over 120% to make up for their loss. The largest daily gain since the DAX was launched in 1988 fell in the period of the crash. On 13 October 2008, four weeks after the Lehman insolvency and five months before the low, the index rose by 11.40%.

In the real economy, German economic output shrank by around 5.7% in 2009. That was the sharpest slump of the post-war period, but thanks to short-time work (Kurzarbeit), unemployment barely rose. In the US, the unemployment rate reached 10% in October 2009. The inflation rate in Germany fell from 2.6% (2008) to 0.3% (2009). In the US, prices actually fell, with the rate dropping from 3.8% to minus 0.4%. At the time, the acute danger was deflation rather than inflation. This is often misrepresented in the later debate about central bank balance sheets.

Some investors recognised the weaknesses of the construction early and bet against it. To do so, they bought credit default insurance ([[Credit default swap|credit default swaps]]) on subprime securitisations. Michael Burry's fund Scion built up this position from 2005 onwards. According to Michael Lewis's account, the fund achieved around 490% after costs from 2000 to 2008. John Paulson's funds earned in the order of $15 billion in 2007.

Until the bets paid off, the premium was due every quarter, while the prices of the securities initially continued to rise. For months, the position therefore brought fixed costs and book losses. Burry had to keep his investors in the fund against their declared wishes. Counterparties valued the positions in their own favour, and several managers with the same view gave up before the bets paid off.

In a portfolio, a correct analysis with the wrong timing cannot be distinguished from a mistake until the expected development occurs. Moreover, this bet could only be entered into with institutional access, master agreements and posted collateral. Each of these gains was matched by the loss of a bank that had sold the insurance, and in the end the taxpayer helped to bear this loss.

bloecke.md: The largest banks are bigger today than in 2008, and the [[Bail-in|bail-in]] has never been tested on one of the large systemically important banks. In supervisory law, government bonds still mostly carry a risk weight of zero. The link between banks and their states therefore persists and is enshrined in the rules. A large part of lending has shifted to funds and other non-banks, to which the new capital rules do not apply. In addition, ratings are still anchored in investment guidelines and supervisory law, even though this anchoring triggered the forced sales in 2007.

- Balances should be limited per institution. Statutory [[Deposit protection|deposit protection]] covers €100,000 per customer and institution (Section 8 EinSiG). After certain life events, such as the sale of a property, a higher limit applies for six months. Balances above these limits are only protected by a voluntary protection scheme, which many banks also belong to. Without one, what remains is an insolvency claim, which for private individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises is satisfied before the other insolvency claims (Section 46f(4) KWG).
- The legal form of a product should be checked before its return. The assets of funds and ETFs are kept separate from the assets of the management company. For German funds, they form [[Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)|segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)]] under Section 92 KAGB (German Investment Code), which do not become part of the management company's insolvency estate if it becomes insolvent (Section 99(3) KAGB). Certificates, by contrast, are bearer bonds (Inhaberschuldverschreibungen). In the Lehman case, this difference decided whether investors bore a price risk or suffered a total loss.
- Your own liquidity is more important than an opinion on price movements. Investors who sold in 2009 rarely did so out of conviction. Mostly they needed money or had to service a loan.
- Investors should know about the tax watershed that fell in the middle of the crisis. The [[Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)|flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] has applied since 1 January 2009. Shares bought before that date remain tax-free when sold. For fund units acquired before 2009, this protection ended on 1 January 2018. For these units, the increases in value up to the end of 2017 remain tax-free, as do later gains up to an allowance of €100,000 per person (Section 56(6) InvStG (Investment Tax Act)).

bloecke.text: We conclude this financial crisis was avoidable.
bloecke.quelle: Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission, final report, January 2011

bloecke.md: The report quoted was backed by six of the ten commission members; four submitted dissenting views. The question of causes also remains open. The explanations put forward include US key interest rates that stayed low for too long after 2001, a global surplus of savings for which safe investments were sought, the deregulation of the 1990s and government promotion of home ownership. Each of these explanations has prominent advocates, and none can be cleanly separated from the others. What is documented is the sequence of the chain and the associated figures, but not the ranking of those responsible.

A risk does not disappear by being bundled, rated and sold on. Afterwards it is harder to recognise, and this makes it bigger. A bank becomes unable to pay when its lenders withdraw its funding, and losses alone do not bring this about.

mitnehmen: The 2008 crisis was above all a funding crisis, because banks with short-term funding and 3% to 5% equity held securities whose value nobody could determine any more.
The safety of an AAA tranche rested solely on the assumption that the loans would not default at the same time, and this assumption came from a period without nationwide falling house prices.
Which financial institution is rescued is a political decision; within half a year, Bear Stearns and AIG were rescued, but Lehman was not.

The S&P 500 and the DAX lost around 55% to 57% and only regained their previous levels after five and a half years, while the strongest daily gain since the DAX was launched in 1988 fell in the middle of the crash.

The crisis gave rise to capital, liquidity and securitisation rules as well as creditor participation in resolutions; the size of the banks, the role of non-banks and the interdependence of banks and states remained unresolved.

begriffe.text: Conversion of a bundle of loans into tradable securities. A special purpose vehicle buys the claims and finances the purchase by issuing securities whose payments come from the loan pool.
Ranking class of a securitised instrument. Interest and repayments flow from the top tranche downwards, while defaults are allocated from the bottom tranche upwards.

Company set up specifically, without any business of its own, which holds and finances assets. Before 2008, it often remained off the bank's balance sheet even though the bank had given guarantees for it.

Contract under which the buyer pays an ongoing premium and receives a compensation payment if a specific borrower or security defaults. Economically it corresponds to credit default insurance; legally it is a derivative without insurance supervision.
Sale of a security with a simultaneous agreement to buy it back, economically a secured loan, often overnight. The haircut determines how much money you receive against a security.
